title: 4/28 first end-of-day health cycle sent a false memory_growth CRITICAL (thresholds set on the sleeping baseline)
tier_reason: one false CRITICAL health DM; no delivery, state or liveness impact attributed to the alert itself (the concurrent unexplained restart is proposed as a separate record)

contract.text: memory_growth raises CRITICAL only for a likely real leak, not for the scheduler's normal post-prediction resident memory.
contract.source: commit 4e221c8 message body (CRITICAL 6144 MB 'likely real leak'); commit e74c485 body (T3 memory_growth)

mechanism.text: memory_growth used INFO 200 / WARN 500 / CRITICAL 1024 MB, calibrated on the ~90 MB sleeping baseline, while the scheduler's in-process prediction path legitimately holds 2-3 GB that CPython does not return; the first end-of-day run therefore reported 2.9 GB as CRITICAL

residual.text: The retuned WARN threshold (3072 MB) still sat inside normal post-prediction RSS (2.8-3.6 GB per the 5/23 walkthrough), mixing cold and post-prediction baselines; recalibrated by 279f190 on 5/23 (E52/I-052).

watchdog.trigger: an NRestarts increase between two end-of-day health runs that no deploy run or date transition explains (the concurrent 0-to-1 restart here); the false CRITICAL itself has no service boundary and is a threshold-calibration matter
watchdog.recovery_assertion: end-of-day health runs on normal days produce no memory CRITICAL and NRestarts stays flat between deploys

evidence.what: the first end-of-day health cycle on 4/28 fired a spurious CRITICAL for the scheduler at 2.9 GB RSS (the 21:21 ET CRITICAL); the misfire also coincided with an unintended scheduler restart (NRestarts 0 to 1), root cause unclear from the journal, possibly a watchdog timeout under high RSS - follow-up deferred
the end-of-day runner sends one Bluesky DM for the aggregated CRITICAL set; memory_growth is a T3 check
deploy-branch push of head 4e221c8 created 2026-04-29T01:25:10Z (4/28 21:25 ET), conclusion success; log unavailable_expired
history showed normal post-prediction RSS around 2.8-3.6 GB while sleeping RSS is about 140 MB; absolute 1 GB/3 GB thresholds mixed the two baselines

notes: split? E38a = this false CRITICAL (B, fixed); E38b = the unexplained scheduler restart during the same end-of-day cycle (NRestarts 0 to 1), which the body defers; E38b would be unresolved_candidate and the journal that could settle it is not retained (journals start 5/11)

I'm guessing on E38b: at 4e221c8's parent the next-day wake was computed as today's 10:00 ET (see I-049), so after the 21:21 health run _idle_until_next_wakeup would no-op, the process would exit cleanly and Restart=always would relaunch it once - after 20:00 ET the relaunch runs the next UTC date, so exactly one restart; code reading only
alert fields not_applicable: the false CRITICAL is the symptom
the restart deferral is not listed as a residual because its mechanism is unknown; it belongs to E38b
